title: Five lines
summary: Meet the stave: higher on the lines means higher in sound.
usSummary: Meet the staff: higher on the lines means higher in sound.

hook.text: Music is written down on five lines. Press play: this tune climbs through them, with one note on each line. Watch where the notes go as the sound gets higher. What do you spot?

explore.text: Press Play. The tune climbs, then falls. Follow the notes with your eyes as you listen. Then play it again and point at each note as it sounds.
explore.goal: Play the tune and follow the notes as they climb and fall.

cards.text: Music is written on a [[stave|stave]]: five [[line|lines]], counted from the bottom up. The bottom line is the first line and the top line is the fifth. The curly sign at the start does a job too, but that comes two lessons from now.
The higher a note sits on the [[stave|stave]], the higher it sounds. This tune falls, so its notes step down the page. Higher sound, higher on the page. Lower sound, lower on the page.

alternative.text: On the keyboard, higher sounds are further to the right. The [[stave|stave]] turns that idea on its side: higher sounds are further up the page. Play the glowing keys from left to right, then picture the notes climbing the lines.
